tagline: 6,000 islands, 227 inhabited — the Mediterranean's original archipelago.
summary: Greece is a nation defined by its sea: roughly 6,000 islands and islets, 227 of them inhabited, scattered across the Aegean and Ionian. Island-hopping is both the backbone of Greek life and one of the world's great travel rituals. Today it runs on large, schedule-bound ferries and high-speed catamarans that pack the summer Cyclades. A clean, on-demand foiling tier is the premium layer between the big-ferry timetable and the private yacht.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief tells the Greek story, because the story IS the Aegean between Santorini, Mykonos, Paros, Naxos and Milos. The summer Cyclades move on crowded fast ferries that sell out and sail on fixed timetables; the alternative is a chartered yacht few can justify. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier slots in between — an on-demand, dry, stabilised crossing that turns the inter-island hop into a smooth 30-to-60-minute glide rather than a queued, weather-tossed ferry ride.

demand_signals.label: Cyclades visitor density
demand_signals.note: Santorini and Mykonos alone draw millions of summer visitors, the overwhelming majority of whom arrive or move by sea between islands.

demand_signals.label: High-net-worth island travel
demand_signals.note: The Cyclades and Ionian are a global luxury-travel and superyacht hub; demand for discreet, fast, premium inter-island transfers is structural.

demand_signals.label: Inhabited-island necessity
demand_signals.note: 227 inhabited islands depend on ferry links for people, goods and tourism — marine transport is core infrastructure, not a discretionary trip.

demand_signals.label: Meltemi schedule risk
demand_signals.note: The summer Meltemi winds routinely disrupt and cancel ferry sailings — exactly the volatility a stabilised foiling craft is built to ride through.

use_cases.body: Santorini to Mykonos: the marquee Cyclades crossing, today a packed high-speed ferry on a fixed timetable — ideal for an on-demand, dry, premium foiling tier.
Paros to Mykonos: a short central-Cyclades hop linking two of the chain's busiest islands, comfortably inside Pioneer II range.
Milos to Paros: a western-Cyclades link for travellers chaining the quieter islands to the central hubs without surrendering to the ferry timetable.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core Cyclades crossings — Santorini–Mykonos (66 nm), Paros–Mykonos (23 nm), Milos–Paros (48 nm) — sit inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Longer Aegean and Ionian trunks (Athens out to the deeper Cyclades, or Dodecanese chains) become Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+) as range comes online.

signature_routes.label: Santorini ↔ Mykonos — the marquee Cyclades crossing

transit_planning: For a tourism authority or a premium operator: an on-demand, low-emission water tier that relieves the timetable bottleneck on the busiest Cyclades crossings, holds a schedule when the Meltemi cancels ferries, and gives the island-hop the comfort of a private craft at a shuttle's cadence. Start with the proven Santorini–Mykonos–Paros triangle on Pioneer II.
competitive_landscape: Island travel today splits between large ferries and high-speed catamarans (affordable, high-capacity, but timetabled, crowded and Meltemi-vulnerable) and private yacht charter (flexible but costly and slow). Navier's foiling tier is the missing on-demand middle: faster and drier than a ferry crossing, far more attainable than a charter, and cleaner than both.
regulatory_note: Greek domestic maritime transport is regulated by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy and the Hellenic Coast Guard, within EU maritime-safety frameworks; passenger operation requires vessel certification and route authorisation. The Cyclades regional port authorities are natural first touchpoints.
seasonality: Peak season (Jun–Sep) brings the strongest demand and the Meltemi winds; the shoulder months (May, Oct) offer calmer seas. A stabilised foiling craft is most differentiated precisely in the windy peak, when conventional fast ferries cancel.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to the Cyclades.
